A KAB glide bomb has limited range, so its carrier aircraft must come close to the front.
Without the A-50's warning of Ukrainian SAMs and fighters, Russian Su-34s and Su-35s "can no longer feel free" (March 2024).
Without the A-50, Russian glide-bomb carriers "no longer dare to fly too close" (March 2024).

cites.quote: no longer dare to fly too close

text: The February 2024 Ukrainian shoot-down spree hit Russian aircraft on glide-bomb runs.
In the Patriot SAMbush a mobile battery is moved forward to the edge of the front, fires at the limit of its kinematics, then leaves.
Defense Express models the SAMbush as a "wandering Patriot" 15–25 km behind the line.
Remote Patriot launchers can sit far forward of the radar, limiting the radar's exposure.
notes: 'limiting the radar's exposure' paraphrases the heading 'Emissions'

text: The 14 January 2024 intercept could also have been cued by passive sensors picking up the A-50's and Il-22's own emissions.
Tom Cooper hypothesises that Ukrainian S-300 radars were switched on only briefly in the January 2024 ambush.
The Times describes Ukrainian S-300 radars being used as bait to draw Russian aircraft into Patriot range.
The S-200 is a huge, old semi-active-homing SAM suited to big, slow targets.
Ukraine restored the S-200, missed once in autumn 2023 when the A-50 turned away, and learned to hide its launchers fast.
Before the 23 February 2024 kill the Ukrainian S-200 waited forward for a week.
Kyiv Post lists possible modifications to Ukraine's S-200 (more fuel, new guidance, a forward illuminator), but they are undisclosed.
In its last seconds on 23 February 2024 the A-50 dropped infrared flares.
The A-50 that evaded the S-200 in autumn 2023 did so by changing course.
Russia's strategic countermeasure to the A-50 ambushes was geographic: moving the orbit east and inland, then deep into Russia.
Oleshchuk published Cospas-Sarsat emergency-beacon positions of downed Russian crews in the Sea of Azov as evidence of the kills.
Over Kyiv in 2022 Russian Su-35S and Su-30SM radars, and R-77-1 shots from over 100 km, outclassed the semi-active R-27s of Ukrainian jets.
Over Kyiv in 2022 Ukrainian pilots were outnumbered by up to 15:2.
Over Kyiv in 2022 Ukrainian pilots flew "extremely low" to use ground clutter and terrain masking.
In 2022 Buk TELARs used as solitary pop-up threats were the best Ukrainian SAMs against Russian jets.
In 2022 MANPADS punished Russian aircraft when they went low.
In 2022 a Russian Podlet-K1 radar in Belarus covered the Kyiv axis down to about 15 ft at over 150 km.
Ukrainian low-level ambushes on high Russian patrols in 2022 suggest the Podlet-K1 radar had low resolution or its picture was poorly disseminated.

counter: moving the A-50 orbit east and inland
measure: Patriot SAMbush on forward A-50 orbits
effect: takes the orbit out of forward Patriot reach at the cost of coverage
rationale: After the 14 January 2024 Patriot ambush Russia moved the A-50 orbit east over land near Krasnodar, trading coverage for survival.

measure: moving the A-50 orbit east and inland
effect: reached the relocated orbit at 200+ km
rationale: Ukraine answered the relocated orbit with a restored S-200 that reached an A-50 over Krasnodar Krai about 200 km or more from the front on 23 February 2024.
In autumn 2023 the first S-200 shot at an A-50 missed when the aircraft turned away.
RUSI found Ukraine could degrade the A-50 'fairly easy' by electronic attack.

counter: very low-level flight using ground clutter and terrain masking
measure: Russian fighter radars and the Podlet-K1 radar
effect: allowed low-level ambushes on high Russian patrols
rationale: Ukrainian pilots flew extremely low to use ground clutter and terrain masking, and low-level ambushes on high Russian patrols worked.

effect: at least 8 aircraft lost in a week; low-level penetration stopped
rationale: When the VKS went low in late February–early March 2022, MANPADS downed at least 8 Su-25/Su-30/Su-34 in a week; low-level penetrating sorties had stopped by April 2022.

text: On the night of 14 January 2024 two Russian tracks settled into orbits: the Il-22M off the Arabat Spit and the A-50 heading for its patrol box off Kyrylivka.
At about 21:00 on 14 January 2024 the Il-22 was hit and turned for Anapa; minutes later the A-50 vanished from the scope and stopped answering, and a Su-30 pilot reported a fire falling into the sea.
Ihnat said the Il-22 was hit on 14 January 2024 while the A-50 was the target, making the engagement a two-for-one.
notes: 'two-for-one' is the dossier's framing of Ihnat's statement

text: In the shoot-and-scoot, a German truck-mounted Patriot runs to the edge of the front, shoots at the kinematic limit and is gone before Russian counter-strikes arrive.
In Zaluzhnyi's flight-track video of 14 January 2024 two tracks "suddenly disappear", near Prymorsk and on the way back to Russia.
Before the 23 February 2024 kill the S-200 crew had waited a week at the front.
On 23 February 2024 an A-50 that took off from Akhtubinsk at 15:50 radiated near Primorsko-Akhtarsk, and at 18:45 its radar died.
Dusk videos of 23 February 2024 show the A-50 dropping flares, then a fireball over Kuban farmland.
After the 23 February 2024 A-50 kill five Russian jets over Millerovo were called home.
On 19 February 2024 Oleshchuk posted emergency-beacon pings from the Sea of Azov; Russian rescuers reported a Su-35 pilot "floating face down", with the Su-34 crew's beacon next to it.
On 13 May 2023 over Bryansk Oblast a Ukrainian Patriot downed a Su-34, a Su-35 and three Mi-8s in five minutes.

observations.value_text: a Su-34, a Su-35 and three Mi-8s
observations.subject: Russian aircraft and helicopters

text: On 26 February 2023 partisan drones reached the A-50 parked at Machulishchy, 12 km from Minsk.
After the 26 February 2023 Machulishchy attack a bag of drone remote controls was found.
Over Kyiv in February–March 2022 Ukrainian MiG-29s and Su-27s hugged the ground under high Su-35 patrols, then popped up to fire.
Ukraine changed its jet–SAM deconfliction rule from time to area after friendly-fire losses on 3 March 2022.
From early March 2022 Buk and S-300 made the high sky lethal for the VKS, and MANPADS made the low sky lethal.
The viral "Ghost of Kyiv" clip was DCS World footage and the "photo" a 2019 Ukrainian MoD image.
The Ukrainian Air Force said the Ghost of Kyiv is "a superhero-legend whose character was created by Ukrainians", a collective image of the 40th Brigade's pilots.

cites.quote: a superhero-legend whose character was created by Ukrainians

text: The Ukrainian Air Force said the fallen Maj. Stepan Tarabalka "is not the Ghost of Kyiv, and he did not shoot down 40 planes".

cites.quote: is not the Ghost of Kyiv, and he did not shoot down 40 planes

notes: the 40-plane figure is denied, so no observation recorded

text: RUSI notes that the "viral pieces of footage" of air-to-air combat over Ukraine in 2022 were "quickly recognisable as fakes created using commercial flight simulator software".

cites.quote: quickly recognisable as fakes created using commercial flight simulator software

measure: Russian counter-strikes on forward SAM batteries
rationale: A German truck-mounted Patriot runs to the edge of the front, shoots and is gone before Russian counter-strikes arrive.

text: In May 2022 Ukraine decided to revive the retired 1960s S-200, finding its old operators and rebuilding launchers and missiles.
The payoff of Ukraine's 2022 decision to restore the S-200 came nearly two years later, in February 2024, at ranges Patriot could not reach.
In November 2023 the UK MoD warned that Russia might accept more risk with the A-50 Mainstay.
Russia decided in early January 2024 to fly constant A-50 sorties, closer to the front, over the threat to Crimea.
The Modern War Institute reads Russia's forward A-50 orbit in January 2024 as urgent need and risk acceptance.

In January 2024 Ukraine chose to use Patriot, a scarce strategic SAM, as a forward ambush weapon rather than for city defence, which a US officer called "stretching the very, very edges" of its envelope.
notes: decision point; alternative was city defence

text: The precedent for Ukraine's forward Patriot ambush was Bryansk in May 2023.
Ihnat says the A-50 was the priority target on 14 January 2024 and the Il-22M was hit in the same engagement ("caught in crossfire"); sources say nothing of an alternative plan.
From 17 January 2024 Russia moved the A-50 orbit east, trading coverage for survival "at the expense of their overall efficacy in Ukraine", in UK Defence Intelligence's words.

cites.quote: at the expense of their overall efficacy in Ukraine

text: In February 2024, rather than chase the new A-50 orbit with Patriot, HUR and the Ukrainian Air Force set an S-200 ambush and waited a week.
notes: decision point; alternative was chasing the orbit with Patriot

text: Ukraine struck the second A-50 on 23 February 2024, Russia's Defender of the Fatherland Day, a date HUR made a point of.
Russia recalled strike sorties on 23–24 February 2024 after losing the A-50.
Russia flew no A-50s near the front for over a week after 23 February 2024, and Oleshchuk reported Russian pilots' "discussions" about being sent "one way".

observations.subject: absence of A-50 near the front

text: In March 2024 Ukraine struck Taganrog, the only A-50 repair plant.
notes: decision point: going after the repair base

text: In December 2024 Ukraine struck Taganrog, the only A-50 repair plant, again.
In November 2025 Ukraine struck Taganrog, the only A-50 repair plant, again.
In June 2025 Operation Spiderweb reached the A-50 home base at Ivanovo.
Over Kyiv in 2022 Ukraine switched jet–SAM deconfliction from time to area after friendly fire.
In 2022 Russian pilots went low, then refused missions beyond the lines, and the VKS switched to night attacks from 9 March.
On 30 April 2022 the Ukrainian Air Force chose to debunk its own "Ghost of Kyiv" myth after The Times misidentified the Ghost.
The Russian MoD did not comment on the 14 January 2024 losses.
UK Defence Intelligence read Russia's eastward A-50 redeployment in January 2024 as "tacit Russian acknowledgement" of the loss.
After 14 January 2024 Russian Telegram channels (Rybar, Colonelcassad, Kotenok and others, as reported) blamed S-400s guarding the Crimean bridge for the A-50 loss.
A self-described Russian security insider called the S-400 friendly-fire story a "duck" (a planted story) meant to reassure pilots that the Azov and Black Sea were still safe.
After 23 February 2024 Russian sources again blamed their own air defence, firing from the Mariupol area, for the A-50 loss.
Russian milbloggers extended the friendly-fire claim to the recent Su-34 and Su-35 losses (February 2024).
ISW judged that if the A-50 really fell to Russian air defence on 14 January 2024, that would itself be "a calamitous failure".
The Russian aviation channel FighterBomber blamed commanders without the right background for the January 2024 losses, published the Il-22's shrapnel damage and called its crew "real heroes".
Military Informant called the January 2024 A-50 loss "a huge loss for domestic aviation".

cites.quote: a huge loss for domestic aviation

text: A Russian milblogger noted that the A-50 and its specialist crews cannot easily be replaced (February 2024).
As Kyiv Post reports it, a Moscow court framed the 23 February 2024 A-50 as patrolling over Krasnodar Krai, "not directly intended for combat operations in Ukraine" and unarmed.

cites.quote: not directly intended for combat operations in Ukraine

text: The Moscow court charged Col. Mykola Dzyaman for an S-200 kill of the 23 February 2024 A-50 at about 300 km.

observations.subject: S-200 kill of the A-50 (Russian court)

text: Lukashenko denied the February 2023 Machulishchy attack, then minimised it, then admitted the A-50 needed repair in Russia.
The Russian MoD claimed 47 drones intercepted on 9 March 2024, 41 of them over Rostov Oblast.
FighterBomber publicised another refurbished A-50U handed over to Russia's air force in May 2026.
